abilities.name: Light Bending
abilities.narrationHints: Curving light around objects or people — partial invisibility, mirages, redirected beams. The edges shimmer like heat haze.
abilities.description: Bend light around yourself or objects — concealment, mirage, or redirection.
abilities.notFor: Affecting anything physical (bent light stops no arrow); working in total darkness (it needs light to bend); undoing what someone already saw.

tree.cannot: Movement breaks it above a slow creep; your shadow stays true; touch reveals everything.

tree.name: Drawn Curtain
tree.grants: Move at walking pace veiled; cloak one companion standing close; project a simple still image (a closed door, an empty shelf) over reality for minutes.
tree.cannot: Images don't survive scrutiny from arm's length; fails under Harmonic sound-sight (echo senses ignore it).

tree.name: Second Sun
tree.grants: Full mirage-craft: a moving figure, a wall that isn't there, daylight in a cellar; split your image into three. And a soundless flash that blinds a group for a breath — while it lasts they cannot aim, cannot follow a movement, and every act that needs their eyes is badly weakened until the glare clears.
tree.cannot: Bent light still stops no arrow. The flash takes friend and foe alike unless they knew to look away, and a Prism-Sight adept reads the bend coming. Blinding is a breath, not a scene — plan what you do with it before you spend it.

abilities.name: Radiant Lance
abilities.narrationHints: A coherent beam of focused light — silent, precise, instantaneous. Leaves clean scorch lines.
abilities.description: Focus light into a searing coherent beam — precise, silent, fast as sight.
abilities.notFor: Subtlety (the line of light is visible to everyone); nonlethal crowd control; cutting what light cannot heat (mirror-finish, running water).

tree.name: Needle Beam
tree.grants: A precise burn at 20 paces: sever a rope, scorch a hand into dropping a weapon, light tinder instantly, mark a surface permanently.
tree.cannot: Cannot penetrate armor or thick wood; one heartbeat of beam per breath; useless in smoke or fog.

tree.name: Cutting Line
tree.grants: Sustained cut: through a door bar, a cart axle, light armor at close range; deflect off a carried mirror to strike around a corner (with a wits check).
tree.cannot: Sustained cutting anchors you in place; the beam-line advertises your exact position; still fog-blind.

tree.name: Sunlance
tree.grants: A single devastating coherent strike — through a stone wall's weak point, a Harmonic shield's first rank, an engine block; can be flared wide as a blinding nonlethal burst instead.
tree.cannot: The line of light is visible to everyone, always — there is no quiet way to do this. Mirror-finish and running water still defeat it. And at full focus it is a killing tool: a Sunlance put through a person is not a wound, and the Blazeborn who carry it are taught to flare it wide before they are taught to narrow it.

mechanic.note: T-II = 2d6 per the locked tierLadder (nMult 2). r1's own number: a precise burn at 20 PACES
mechanic.penetrationNote: penetration 2 is derived from the craft's OWN rank text, not chosen: r2 cuts 'LIGHT ARMOR at close range' and r3 goes through 'a HARMONIC SHIELD'S FIRST RANK'. Harmonic's resonant_shield is authored at soakRank 1/2/3 by rank, so a lance that beats its FIRST rank and light armour is penetration 2 — it cuts rank-1 and rank-2 layers and is stopped by resonant_shield r3 (soakRank 3). That is exactly the ranked counter-pair both traditions describe, and it means neither craft is a flat hard-counter: who wins depends on which rank each has reached.

abilities.plainly: A radiant working that stores light in vessels for later release. It fills from any light source, fastest in direct noon sun and slowest by lantern, so it is always gaining something. Another radiant can aim a light craft at the vessels to convert their own energy into charge. While worn it also drinks light-type damage aimed at you and turns it into charge — only light; shadow and edges pass through. It holds up to its rank's capacity; past that you get about two hours of warning, then it bursts for 6d6 on everyone who can see it, blinding them for the scene and destroying the vessel — cover blocks it, since it travels by sight. You can instead tap and channel the excess as a working of your own aiming; failing that check vents half and you take the rest. A charged vessel can be carried off by someone else.

upkeep.onInterrupt: nothing is lost — the vessels keep what they hold and resume

fedByCraft.note: ⚠️ ERIK: a Radiant can BEAM INTO A WELL to charge it fast. Any light-type craft aimed at a vessel converts its energy into charge at half an hour per point, capped at a day's worth per scene. That is a real decision — spend your own pool now to have a full Well sooner — and it makes two Radiants together far more than twice one.

absorbs.note: ⚠️ ERIK: the Well is also a DEFENCE. Light aimed at the bearer is drunk instead of landing, and the harm becomes charge. It answers only LIGHT — a shadow or an edge goes straight through — so it is a counter to one thing rather than armour.

upkeep.note: a rate, not a gate: the Well is never idle, and prepHours are direct-noon equivalents

overcharge.warning: the vessels ring faintly and the light in them stops being still

onBurst.area: everyone within sight of the vessels
onBurst.alsoBlinds: all who see it, for the scene

overcharge.note: ⚠️ ERIK: 'a light well that gets overcharged could potentially blow up catastrophically.' It does. Past capacity there is a two-hour grace where the vessels WARN — they ring, and the light stops being still — and then it bursts for 6d6 light on everyone in sight, blinds them for the scene, and the vessel is gone. Note it hits BY SIGHT, not by radius: taking cover behind something opaque is the counterplay, which is exactly right for light.

venting.onSuccess: the excess is spent as a released working — full effect, your choosing of target
venting.onFailure: you vent half and take the rest yourself
venting.note: ⚠️ ERIK: 'unless the user is able to tap it and channel the output.' So overcharge is not a punishment, it is a DECISION UNDER PRESSURE: a Radiant who sees the ring coming can spend the excess deliberately and get a very large working out of it. THE BEST USE OF THE WELL IS TO DELIBERATELY OVERFILL IT AND THEN AIM IT, and the risk of getting that wrong is the price.

takeable.worth: valuable while charged, trivial when empty
takeable.note: ⚠️ ERIK: 'yes a charged vessel is takeable.' A full Well is portable stored power and worth stealing — and a thief who does not know the capacity is carrying something that will burst. That is a good hook rather than a griefing problem, because the danger travels with the prize.
